CASE_STUDY.TITLE: Leading Financial Institution Goes Experiential
CASE_STUDY.SUMMARY: Terragni helped a top‑3 financial institution improve engagement, loyalty and profitability through experiential segmentation and differentiated experiences.
CASE_STUDY.CHALLENGE: High friction loyalty tracking, low utilization of wealth products, low acquisition and a one‑size‑fits‑all onboarding process.
CASE_STUDY.OBJECTIVE: Design & deliver signature differentiated experiences that drive higher customer engagement.
CASE_STUDY.APPROACH: Conducted phenomenological in‑depth interviews, consumer‑neuroscience assessments and experiential segmentation to uncover customer expectations.
CASE_STUDY.KEY_FINDING: Customers fall into four experiential segments based on capability and time willingness (high/low capability × high/low time).
CASE_STUDY.SOLUTION: Created tailored experiences for each segment, enhanced the loyalty program and personalized onboarding.
CASE_STUDY.BUSINESS_OUTCOME: Increased wallet share, increased customer acquisition through recommendation, increased customer retention, reduced cost to serve.

CASE_STUDY.TITLE: Life Insurance in Tier 2 and Tier 3
CASE_STUDY.SUMMARY: Terragni helped a private life insurance player improve retention and persistency among Tier 2 and Tier 3 customers.
CASE_STUDY.CHALLENGE: Customers defecting at 37% among the top 4 players in the private life insurance sector.
CASE_STUDY.APPROACH: Automated reminders, rewards linked to life goals, and timely nudges using the EAST framework to encourage consistent premium payments.
CASE_STUDY.SOLUTION: Tailored communication and frictionless support combined with behavioural nudges to drive payment consistency.
CASE_STUDY.BUSINESS_OUTCOME: Increased customer retention, improved persistency, enhanced digital adoption, reduced cost of service, and better customer connect and contactibility.

CASE_STUDY.TITLE: Driving Customer Engagement for Affluent Banking

CASE_STUDY.BUSINESS_OUTCOME: Increased wallet share, increased customer acquisition through recommendation, increased customer retention.

CASE_STUDY.TITLE: Bajaj Allianz Life Insurance - Barriers to Premium Renewals - Pilot
CASE_STUDY.SUMMARY: Pilot study examining barriers to premium renewals for Bajaj Allianz Life Insurance across two geographies.
CASE_STUDY.CHALLENGE: Customers experience digital touchpoint issues, uncooperative representatives, and lack flexibility in premium payment options.
CASE_STUDY.APPROACH: Used the EAS‑Pilot framework to assess effort dimensions (physical, time, cognitive) and assign process levels (Enhancer, Enabler, Low Ease, etc.) with redesign recommendations.
CASE_STUDY.KEY_FINDING: 52% of respondents cannot change premium payment frequency; 1 in 2 customers face digital issues; physical channels dominate premium payment effort.
CASE_STUDY.SOLUTION: Recommend process redesign to lower effort levels, increase payment flexibility, improve digital touchpoints, and provide clearer communication.

CASE_STUDY.TITLE: ABHI Behaviours for Business
CASE_STUDY.SUMMARY: Study of ABHI's transaction friction, post‑purchase experience and segment‑specific engagement strategies.
CASE_STUDY.CHALLENGE: Transaction experience sees friction across the engagement lifecycle, with longer response times and perception of being sales‑focused.
CASE_STUDY.APPROACH: Segment‑wise sales approaches and a Marketing Aircover using nudges and health‑champion programs.
CASE_STUDY.SOLUTION: Implementation of tiered Health Champion program, FlexiHealth customization, and tribe‑based nudges.

CASE_STUDY.TITLE: Behaviours for Business - Driving market share and wallet share for premium banking among affluent customer segment
CASE_STUDY.SUMMARY: A Terragni case study focused on increasing market share and wallet share for premium banking among existing and potential affluent customers.
CASE_STUDY.CHALLENGE: Low customer acquisition & engagement among affluent segments; weak word-of-mouth; premium banking perceived as lacking relevance and high friction.
CASE_STUDY.OBJECTIVE: Drive higher acquisition and engagement of affluent customers, boost word-of-mouth, and increase retention through greater utilization of premium banking.
CASE_STUDY.APPROACH: Implemented intermediate tiered program, experiential segmentation, redefined RM role, white‑glove experiences, behavioral nudges, journey mapping, process blueprinting, and service recovery.
CASE_STUDY.KEY_FINDING: Affluent customers want investment growth, lifestyle experiences, and status, but find current benefits high effort, low value, and poorly aligned with life goals.
CASE_STUDY.SOLUTION: Strategic and operational solutions combining tiered loyalty, contextual segmentation, proactive RM engagement, frictionless experiences, and behavioral design.
CASE_STUDY.BUSINESS_OUTCOME: Increased program utilization, organic affluent acquisition, social proof, word‑of‑mouth, and wallet share among existing affluent customers.

CASE_STUDY.TITLE: Leading Financial Institution Goes Experiential For Wealth Management

associations and emotional
components of effort for two

Terragni Sensemaking
While traditional research focuses on stated preferences and subjective choices, our Sensemaking approach
integrates Consumer Neuroscience, Behavioural Science, Traditional & Secondary Research, and Domain
Knowledge, to uncover deep, context-specific, non-conscious drivers of behaviours and decisions.
This enables brands to optimize brand and product positioning, and drive accurate testing, stronger adoption,
and sustained loyalty and wallet share—leading to superior business outcomes.

Traditional research relies on what humans explicitly express; Sensemaking delves into what humans implicitly
feel.
How?
Uncovers Hidden Associations – Products and their usage evoke context specific associations. These
determine customer decisions and subsequent repurchase and loyalty.
Sharper Brand Positioning – Implicit tests reveal the “gut-level” associations people have with your brand;
associations that often shape perceptions before logic and rationalization kicks in. This reveals positioning
opportunities that traditional research may miss out on.
In-depth, Actionable Insights – most research captures what people think they think. IAT captures what
they actually feel and are unaware of. It bridges the gap between stated intent and real-world behaviour.
Robust Predictions – The IAT captures fast automatic responses- bypassing post rationalization and social
desirability bias. This leads to more accurate behaviour prediction, requiring leaner sample sizes.

Strategic Solutions
• Intermediate premium program to build loyalty early: An
intermediate tiered program with early access, milestone unlocks,
and upgrade nudges. When rising affluent customers feel
recognized before they qualify for the premium banking program,
it boosts loyalty and turns rising affluents into potential premium
customers.
• Experiential segmentation by context and goals: Current
customer segmentation overlooks behavioural and life-stage
diversity. Introduced Experiential Segments based on evolving
contextual needs (e.g., legacy planning, entrepreneurial expansion)
to guide service personalization and help customers feel seen
beyond their assets. (E.g. NRI Pioneers, Adjacent Alliances, Elite
Affluents)

Strategic Solutions
• RMs as proactive enablers, not passive product sellers: Redefined
RMs’ role to drive goal-aligned nudges by positioning them as
financial life partners through structured outreach cadences,
behaviourally-timed touchpoints, and strategic life-stage check-ins.
• High-prestige, frictionless ‘White Glove’ experiences: Affluent
customers value distinction. Designed exclusive but low effort
rituals like personalized portfolio walkthroughs at key life junctures,
RM-driven gestures, and legacy recognition features building
identity alignment and pride in association.
• Eliminate high-friction moments in high-stakes journeys: For
critical moments like onboarding or fund transfers, we redesigned
affluent customer journeys to minimize paperwork, waiting time,
and ambiguity, especially at high-stakes emotional "peak" moments.

STEPPS* Framework

Social Currency: People share things that make them look good or exclusive.

Triggers: External cues prompt people to talk about certain topics.

Emotion: Strong emotions, positive or negative, make content more shareable.

Public: Observable behaviors encourage others to imitate.

Practical Value: Useful information gets shared to help others.

Stories: Relatable narratives stick and are easily shared.

Terragni Sensemaking
While traditional research focuses on stated preferences and subjective choices, our Sensemaking approach
integrates Consumer Neuroscience, Behavioural Science, Traditional & Secondary Research, and Domain
Knowledge, to uncover deep, context-specific, non-conscious drivers of behaviours and decisions.
This enables brands to optimize brand and product positioning, and drive accurate testing, stronger adoption,
and sustained loyalty and wallet share—leading to superior business outcomes.

Traditional research relies on what humans explicitly express; Sensemaking delves into what humans implicitly
feel.
How?
Uncovers Hidden Associations – Products and their usage evoke context specific associations. These
determine customer decisions and subsequent repurchase and loyalty.
Sharper Brand Positioning – Implicit tests reveal the “gut-level” associations people have with your brand;
associations that often shape perceptions before logic and rationalization kicks in. This reveals positioning
opportunities that traditional research may miss out on.
In-depth, Actionable Insights – most research captures what people think they think. IAT captures what
they actually feel and are unaware of. It bridges the gap between stated intent and real-world behaviour.
Robust Predictions – The IAT captures fast automatic responses- bypassing post rationalization and social
desirability bias. This leads to more accurate behaviour prediction, requiring leaner sample sizes.
